selected.name: Genuine comic invention performed by this text
selected.instruction: Read the item and ask what act of comic construction it performs: does some specific connection, reversal, mis-reading or reframing get built here, such that a reader who follows the setup arrives somewhere they had not already been carried to? Score 10 when the text does real inventive work -- the pivot creates a link between two things that the setup made available but did not announce, and the payload follows from that link rather than being asserted. A three-word, plainly worded, entirely unfashionable line with no unusual vocabulary and no proper nouns can score 10 if its pivot is genuinely constructed. Score 0 when nothing is constructed: the item merely occupies the shape of a joke, states a topic and then states an attitude toward it, or reproduces a payload that the setup already fully implied, so no step is taken. Explicitly do NOT reward unfamiliarity, obscurity, odd wording, edginess, length, or the mere fact that you have not seen the item before; a phrasing you have never encountered that performs no construction scores 0, and a construction you happen to have met before still scores on the construction itself. Judge the work done in the text, not its novelty as an artifact.
selected.rationale: The upstream cause behind P01 -- someone actually writing rather than copying -- produces two separable things: real construction, and the fingerprint of being unrecognisable. This component keeps only the construction, and forces the judge to name the step the text takes. Dissociation, direction one: a garbled, never-before-seen string of surreal proper nouns with no pivot is maximally unrecognisable (high surface) yet builds nothing (0 here). Direction two: a plain, widely repeated two-line exchange whose punch genuinely turns on a double meaning the setup planted scores high here while being fully recognisable (low surface). The instruction bans the novelty cue explicitly so the judge cannot substitute it.

selected.name: Extent of overlap with stock circulated joke material
selected.instruction: This is a counting question about textual familiarity, not a quality judgement. Estimate 0-10 how much of the item's material -- its frame, its wording, and its payload -- matches joke material that has been in wide circulation. Consider: (a) is the opening frame a stock template you can name (bar-entry, light-bulb, knock-knock, 'what do you call a', 'my wife and I', 'a man walks into'); (b) can you complete or approximately predict the final line before reaching it; (c) does the wording match a canonical version phrase-for-phrase. Score 10 when frame, wording and payload are all standard circulated material you could recite. Score 5 when one of the three is standard and the others are not. Score 0 when none of the three matches anything in circulation you can identify. Do NOT decide whether being familiar or being unfamiliar is good, funny, lazy or skilled; do not consider whether the item works. A completely inert, unfunny, freshly typed line with no recognisable frame scores 0 here, and a beautifully executed line that is word-for-word a classic scores 10 here.
selected.rationale: This is the pure carrier: recognisability of the strings, with all merit removed and all evaluative language banned. Dissociation, direction one: a novel-sounding word salad scores 0 here and 0 on the real component -- absence of the marker guarantees nothing. Direction two: a well-known template filled with a payload that is genuinely constructed in context scores 10 here and high on the real component. Because the scale asks only for degree of match against circulated strings, an item can max it while performing no comic work at all.

selected.name: Setup supplies exactly what the punch needs to land
selected.instruction: Judge only whether the information needed for the joke's mechanism is present and correctly placed, in context. Ask: when the final line arrives, has the text already given the reader every premise, referent and detail that line depends on -- and has it withheld the thing the line reveals? Score 10 when the setup is complete and load-bearing: every pronoun has an antecedent, every referent the punch turns on has been introduced, nothing the punch needs arrives too late, and nothing that would spoil the punch arrives too early. A misspelt, lowercase, unpunctuated, run-on item can score 10 here if its logical scaffolding is intact and the punch has everything it needs. Score 0 when the mechanism cannot resolve: the punch relies on a fact, character or setting never supplied, an 'it' or 'he' points at nothing, the text stops before the mechanism completes, or the payload was already given away in the setup so nothing remains to land. Explicitly do NOT score spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, paragraph breaks, markup artifacts, or the polish of the prose; do NOT score whether the joke is funny -- an unfunny joke whose logic is fully supplied scores 10.
selected.rationale: P02 fuses two things a careful poster produces: prose hygiene, and an actually complete comic mechanism. This keeps the mechanism and bans the hygiene cues by name. Dissociation, direction one: a flawlessly typed, correctly punctuated item whose punch hinges on a character never mentioned scores 10 on surface and 0 here. Direction two: a phone-typed line with three typos and no capitals whose setup plants exactly the ambiguity the punch exploits scores low on surface and 10 here. The scale is about sufficiency of supplied premises, which typing care neither guarantees nor is required for.
member_names: Setup supplies exactly what the punch needs to land

selected.name: Extent of clean mechanical text hygiene
selected.instruction: Count mechanical surface defects only; this is an extent question, not a quality judgement. Scan the text for: misspellings, missing or wrong punctuation, absent or erratic capitalisation, doubled or missing spaces, stray markup or escape characters, broken or absent line breaks where a format needs them, mid-sentence truncation, duplicated fragments, and non-English or garbled character runs. Score 10 when there are no such defects at all: every word is correctly spelled, sentences are correctly punctuated and capitalised, and the text begins and ends cleanly. Score 5 for a handful of defects that a reader passes over. Score 0 when defects are dense or the text is visibly truncated or corrupted. Do NOT decide whether clean typing is good, whether the errors are charming or sloppy, whether the item is comprehensible, or whether it is funny. An empty, pointless, perfectly typed sentence scores 10 here; a brilliant, fully comprehensible joke typed with no capitals and four misspellings scores low here.
selected.rationale: This is the fingerprint alone -- typographic care, countable without reading for sense. Dissociation, direction one: perfect orthography wrapped around a setup that omits the premise the punch needs gives 10 here and 0 on the real component. Direction two: a typo-riddled item with a complete, well-ordered mechanism gives a low score here and 10 there. Every term in the list is a character-level property, so no amount of comic substance can raise it and no amount of sloppiness can lower the substantive twin.
member_names: Extent of clean mechanical text hygiene

selected.name: Economy and timing of information release before the punch
selected.instruction: Judge the handling of information in this specific text, whatever shape it takes. Ask: is every element before the final beat doing work, and does the decisive element arrive last? Score 10 when the text is economical and correctly timed for its own content -- no sentence could be deleted without breaking the mechanism, no detail is repeated, no explanation follows the punch, no signposting tells the reader in advance what kind of turn is coming, and the word or phrase that flips the meaning sits at or near the end where it flips the most. A rambling-looking narrative can score 10 if each digression is a plant the ending uses; a one-line item can score 0 if half of it is redundant. Score 0 when the text wastes the reader: filler preamble, the same beat stated twice, the mechanism explained after it fires, or the revealing element buried in the middle so the ending merely restates it. Explicitly do NOT reward conformity to any template, do NOT reward shortness for its own sake, do NOT reward speaker labels, tidy layout or list formatting, and do NOT judge whether the item is funny; a flat joke with perfect information timing scores 10, and a hilarious one that explains itself afterwards scores low.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause -- accumulated practice writing for this forum -- yields both genuine control of pacing and the visible habit of hitting a template exactly. This isolates the control: it is defined over the item's own content (deletability, plant-payoff, position of the flip), so no template can satisfy it by construction. Dissociation, direction one: a textbook-clean question-and-answer riddle that answers itself in the question, then appends a parenthetical explanation, scores 10 on surface and near 0 here. Direction two: a format-mixing item that starts as narration and ends in unlabelled dialogue, but whose every clause is a plant the last four words cash in, scores low on surface and 10 here.

selected.name: Extent of strict conformity to one recognisable joke template
selected.instruction: Identify which single template, if any, the text is attempting -- pure one-liner, question-and-answer riddle, knock-knock, scripted dialogue with speaker labels, narrative build, or numbered/bulleted list -- then score 0-10 for how strictly it holds that template from first word to last. Score 10 when exactly one template is used with no deviation: the structural slots the template requires are all present, in order, with nothing from another template mixed in and nothing appended after the closing slot (no author commentary, no 'edit:', no tag line, no emoji sign-off). Score 5 when a template is recognisable but broken somewhere -- narration spliced into a riddle, a missing speaker label, a stray remark after the final slot. Score 0 when no template is identifiable and the text has no formal shape. This is a structural conformity count only: do NOT judge whether the chosen template suits the material, whether the closing slot is well filled, or whether the item is funny. A completely flat, unfunny question-and-answer riddle in immaculate two-line form scores 10 here.
selected.rationale: This is the practiced poster's visible fingerprint -- template discipline -- with all craft judgement stripped, and it is scorable by pattern-matching slots without understanding the content. Dissociation, direction one: an immaculate but self-spoiling riddle takes 10 here and near 0 on the timing component. Direction two: a shape-mixing item with flawless plant-and-payoff timing takes a low score here and a high one there. The instruction forbids the judge from asking whether the template was the right choice, which is where merit would otherwise leak in.

selected.name: References are load-bearing, not decorative name-drops
selected.instruction: For every shared reference the item invokes -- a named person, a product, a platform, a news event, a place, or an ordinary shared experience such as commuting or a doctor's waiting room -- ask whether the joke's mechanism actually exploits a specific property of it. Score 10 when each reference is load-bearing: the punch turns on something particular and true about that referent, and swapping it for a different referent of the same category would break the joke. An item containing no proper nouns, no slang and no topical material at all can score 10 if the ordinary shared situation it uses is exploited this precisely. Score 0 when references are decorative: the named person, brand or platform is interchangeable with any other, present only as recognition bait or to set a scene, and the punch would survive unchanged if you substituted a different name. Explicitly do NOT reward how many references there are, how current or recognisable they are, or how fashionable the vocabulary is; a single dense cluster of very recognisable names, none of which is exploited, scores 0. Do NOT judge whether the item is funny -- judge only whether its references do work.
selected.rationale: The conjectured cause behind P04 is when the item was submitted, which co-produces two things: material that engages what readers actually hold in common, and a countable dusting of period markers. This component keeps the engagement and defines it by a substitution test the judge can apply to any item, including ones with no era markers whatsoever. Dissociation, direction one: a line stuffed with a current politician, a current platform and three current slang terms, all interchangeable, scores 10 on surface and 0 here. Direction two: a timeless line about waiting on hold, containing not one dated token, whose punch depends on a specific true property of hold music, scores 0 on surface and 10 here.
member_names: References are load-bearing, not decorative name-drops

selected.name: Extent of dated period markers present in the text
selected.instruction: Count period-specific tokens; this is an extent estimate, not a quality judgement. Tally occurrences of: named public figures tied to a particular era, specific news events or controversies, named products, brands, apps, sites or platforms, platform-native conventions (hashtags, handles, upvote/karma talk, subreddit or thread references, emoji-as-punctuation), prices or technologies that date the text, and slang or idiom characteristic of a particular period. Score 10 when such markers are dense -- several distinct ones, or the whole premise rests on one specific dated event or platform. Score 5 for one or two incidental markers. Score 0 when the text contains none and could have been written in any decade. Do NOT decide whether being dated or being timeless is good, whether the reference is well used, whether it is obscure, or whether the item is funny. A pointless sentence that merely lists three current celebrity names scores 10 here; a superbly crafted joke about a chicken crossing a road scores 0 here.
selected.rationale: This is the timing fingerprint alone: a tally of tokens, decidable without following the joke's logic, and explicitly barred from any judgement of use or worth. Dissociation, direction one: dense interchangeable name-dropping maxes this and bottoms out the load-bearing component. Direction two: a reference-free joke that precisely exploits an everyday shared situation scores 0 here and 10 there. Holding both scales lets a discount of era-marker density be applied without discounting the engagement that the same submission timing also produces.
member_names: Extent of dated period markers present in the text
